title: Breaking the Sky Sword Saint
html:
After the quasi-upper-grade dokkaebi assessment ended, Bihyung somehow grew lazy.

All he did was manage the ‘Korean Peninsula Scenarios’ that Baram, the former Seoul branch chief, had left in his care. And occasionally lie around like this, watching the scenarios he had made.

―Heewon-ssi! Over here!

―Damn it, one got away. Someone head north! Just one person!

On the screen, ‘Whack-a-Mole,’ one of the Korean Peninsula Scenarios, was in full swing. A scenario in which they had to catch every escaped ‘Bomb Mole’ within the allotted time.

Let even one escape, and a horrific explosion would devastate the surrounding area, but the constellations of the Korean Peninsula did not look particularly anxious.

―Titano found it, I'm told. Yoosung and I will handle it.

Incarnations with a perfect lineup and perfect teamwork. They were certainly different from those in some countries where a quarter of the territory had been blown away by similar scenarios.

Of course, that did not mean this scenario was fiendishly difficult, either.

“Damn it, how did things end up like this······?”

Bihyung muttered the complaint, gnawing at his finger.

In truth, he could have made this scenario as difficult as he pleased.

He could have blown away half the peninsula and led every incarnation into a horrific disaster.

But he could not bring himself to do it.

‘Should I have kept Kim Dokja alive back then after all······? If I make this any harder, they'll all fucking die.’

It was too late for regrets now.

No matter how many arrangements he had prepared, it was nearly impossible for someone who had left the scenarios to return alive.

[The constellations of the Korean Peninsula are cheering on ‘Kim Dokja's party.’]

[The constellations of the Korean Peninsula have sponsored 2000 coins.]

Bihyung's channel was still afloat thanks to the ‘diehard subscribing constellations’ Kim Dokja had left behind. Constellations who steadily offered sponsorship, whether the scenarios were interesting or not.

But those were not the only constellations in the channel.

[Many constellations are bored with the scenario's progress.]

[Some constellations have left the channel.]

After Kim Dokja disappeared, and even Yoo Joonghyuk left the Korean Peninsula Scenarios, more viewers abandoned the channel each day.

In a word, Bihyung's channel was slowly going under.

‘I need to make a change. But how?’

Of course, he knew how.

If he cranked the scenarios' difficulty back up to fiendish levels and had the incarnations ground to pieces, the number of subscribing constellations would rise again.

But Bihyung no longer wanted to run his scenarios that way.

‘Maybe I've changed, too.’

Something had changed since the days when he pursued nothing but sensational scenarios and did not care one whit whether the incarnations lived or died. Bihyung wanted to tell a slightly different story. To forget the ‘cathartic payoffs’ the Bureau clamored for day after day and see a different kind of scenario.

Something the constellations could remember for a long, long time, like the scenarios the first generation of dokkaebis had made in the distant past······.

―Bihyung.

When a voice came through Dokkaebi Communication out of thin air, Bihyung reflexively rose to his feet.

―You look quite comfortable. Have you been well?

The face that then appeared on the panel belonged to Baram, the former Seoul branch chief who had left the Seoul Dome upon becoming a ‘Great Dokkaebi Candidate.’ Alarmed, Bihyung hurriedly adopted a respectful manner.

After leaving the Seoul branch, Baram had joined the Bureau's Council of Elders. The council said to gather only the wisest dokkaebis in the world.

Whatever stories he had seen and heard in the meantime, Baram seemed even more dignified through the panel.

―I contacted you because I have a few things to pass along.

“What things······?”

Bihyung grew a little tense. Whenever Baram began with such a portentous opening, the news had never been good.

―There are signs of a Giant Story.

“······But there should still be quite some time before <Gigantomachia> or <Ragnarok>, shouldn't there?”

―Neither of those. This time, the Giant Story will begin in the ‘Demon Realm.’

At the mention of the Demon Realm, Bihyung's expression changed.

“Don't tell me it's the ‘Demon King Selection’?”

Seeing Baram nod, Bihyung swallowed hard.

Unlike the Giant Stories held as regular events, the ‘Demon King Selection’ was an exceedingly rare scenario. Even Bihyung had never witnessed a ‘Demon King Selection’ scenario himself.

‘The last Demon King Selection was already 800 years ago.’

To think that merely imagining a ‘Giant Story’ could make his heart pound like this.

As though he had read Bihyung's thoughts, Baram smiled.

―Doesn't it excite you?

“It does, but it's a shame. Dokkaebis don't handle that region anyway, do they?”

The Demon Realm had long been the territory of the Wenny men. A barren land, practically the only place in the entire scenario zone where channels did not open. That was the ‘Demon Realm.’ So once again, those broadcasting the ‘Demon King Selection’ would be······.

―This time is different. The Bureau has decided to dispatch dokkaebis to the Demon Realm.

“What? But that's······.”

Dokkaebis did not interfere in the affairs of Wenny men, and Wenny men did not interfere in the affairs of dokkaebis. That was the ‘Horizon Pledge.’ Yet what Baram was saying now directly contradicted that pact.

―Originally, we planned to open channels after reaching a new agreement with the Wenny men, but things have become a little complicated. They broke the pledge first.

“They broke the pledge?”

―An ‘illegal channel’ has appeared in the Demon Realm.

“······What?”

By any ordinary reckoning, it was impossible.

There were no dokkaebis in the Demon Realm.

So what did he mean, a ‘channel’ had opened?

―We don't know the details yet. It's thrown the Bureau into an uproar.

“If the Wenny men stole a channel, couldn't we simply shut it down?”

The right to operate channels had always been restricted to dokkaebis.

Even if a Wenny man had used some bizarre trick to steal a channel, the Bureau could easily shut down one or two channels.

―The problem is, it isn't a Wenny man.

“It isn't a Wenny man? Then who opened the channel?”

―There appears to be a dokkaebi in the Demon Realm.

“······A dokkaebi?”

Wait······ Could it be?

No, no. There was no way.

Baram continued.

―At any rate, that is why the Bureau is dispatching dokkaebis to the Demon Realm.

“I see. But why are you telling me······?”

―You're on the dispatch list, too.

“I'm in charge of the Korean Peninsula.”

―Other dokkaebis will take over the peninsula for a while. Take some intermediate- and low-grade dokkaebis with you for a brief visit to the Demon Realm.

For a moment, Bihyung was dumbfounded.

Leave Earth's scenarios, the hottest ones of all, and go to the Demon Realm?

This was as good as a demotion.

―Nothing is happening on the peninsula anyway, is it? Don't take it too hard. If you accomplish something worthwhile this time, a promotion to upper grade won't be just a dream.

“······I seem to recall you saying something similar last time. Why me, of all people?”

―I don't know the exact reason myself, but the Council of Elders specifically chose you.

If the Council of Elders had decided, there would be no reversing it.

Bihyung's face fell.

He had to go to that dangerous place now, of all times?

―I know what you're thinking, but don't be so discouraged. This isn't a demotion. Besides, there's an unusual piece of information you might be pleased to hear.

Bihyung looked up without much hope, and Baram spoke in a curious tone.

―We've received a report that the ‘Demon King of Salvation’ has appeared in the Demon Realm.

●

After my long silence, I finally spoke a full 30 minutes after Yoo Joonghyuk had said those words. I only realized that 30 minutes had passed because Aileen came into the room and left once in the meantime.

“······Yoo Joonghyuk, did you happen to bring the Uriel doll?”

At my question, Yoo Joonghyuk silently took the doll out from inside his clothes.

I carefully accepted the doll and examined it.

Uriel, with the stitching on her arms and legs all torn out.

Even if this was only a symbolic body, damage this severe would have hurt her true body as well.

For that fiercely proud archangel to suffer such treatment in the Demon Realm.

“······I really can't go back yet.”

“I see.”

An answer that sounded as though he had expected it.

When I looked up, Yoo Joonghyuk was also looking at the Uriel doll. Neither of us spoke, but we knew exactly what the other was thinking.

“You're planning to enter the Demon King Selection, aren't you?”

“······That's right.”

The Demon King Selection.

A scenario I had to go through to prepare for the coming confrontations with the constellations.

“I feel bad for the others, but I have to obtain a Giant Story here.”

I continued as I carefully fitted Uriel's torn arm back into place.

“That's how I'll be able to prepare for the Great Destruction Scenarios ahead.”

If I returned to Earth, my options would be limited.

I could still find fortuitous opportunities there and build up a force, but going back at this point would be inefficient.

The scenarios were already more fiendishly difficult than at any point in the original novel.

Returning to Earth now would only waste my time on unrelated matters.

Yoo Joonghyuk watched me for a moment, then spoke.

“Not a bad idea.”

His tone suggested that he understood a great deal.

Yoo Joonghyuk probably understood this feeling better than anyone.

After all, he was probably the one who had lost more things precious to him than anyone else because he was weak.

“What are you going to do?”

“I'll remain in the Demon Realm for the time being, too. I have a personal scenario here, so I can't leave right away.”

Oh, so that was how it was.

“Really? Then why don't you help me, if you don't mind?”

“You're the one who'll be helping me.”

Wondering what he meant, I looked up at Yoo Joonghyuk.

His face was just as expressionless as before, yet something felt different.

“······Don't tell me you're entering the ‘Demon King Selection,’ too?”

“You're stating the obvious.”

Suddenly, my thoughts became tangled. This bastard had planned to enter the ‘Demon King Selection’ all along, so why had he told me······?

“Wait! When you told me to go back to Earth earlier, were you······?”

Without even hearing me out, Yoo Joonghyuk rose and walked over to the window.

The faint sunset cast deep shadows across the side of his face.

According to ‘Ways of Survival,’ Yoo Joonghyuk deliberately made himself look cool when his true intentions were exposed.

So that was it. This bastard had been planning to send me back to Earth and become the Demon King himself.

Looking at his shameless back, I felt all the emotion he had stirred in me vanish.

Then Yoo Joonghyuk spoke.

“They're here.”

As a chill swept in through the window, Aileen and Mark burst through the treatment room door.

I knew what was happening without needing to be told.

Because Biyoo, who had opened her eyes before I knew it, was looking up at me with a tense expression.

[The constellation ‘Founder of Humanity’ is glaring at the ‘Yoo Joonghyuk Industrial Complex.’]

[The constellation ‘Last Pharaoh’ is glaring at the ‘Yoo Joonghyuk Industrial Complex.’]

[Constellations from a certain nebula are glaring at the ‘Yoo Joonghyuk Industrial Complex.’]

Over ten stars seemed to glitter in the sky, before one in particular flared with brilliant light and erupted in sparks.

Bzzzzzt!

A moment later, an enormous figure began to appear at the entrance to the industrial complex. The direct descent of an incarnation body. An enormous mummy with a golden crown on its head. At the sight of its size, towering far above the walls, the incarnations of the complex screamed in unison.

If I remembered correctly, that constellation belonged to <Papyrus>.

And <Papyrus> had allied with the [Bercan] Industrial Complex.

Yoo Joonghyuk spoke as though grinding out each word.

“······Looks like they've come to make a show of force.”

There was no need to ask what sort of show.

The preliminary clash of the Demon King Selection had already begun.

[Who is··· the new ruler··· of this industrial complex?]

At that tremendous voice, Yoo Joonghyuk and I looked out the window at the same time.

Judging by all the crackling static, this one seemed to find using True Voice quite a struggle. Yoo Joonghyuk murmured quietly.

“A constellation from <Papyrus>.”

“If it's the ‘Last Pharaoh,’ it's probably the woman I'm thinking of, right?”

An enormous mummy with an old golden crown. A face with only the high bridge of its nose exposed, everything else covered in bandages. Just as I had read in ‘Ways of Survival.’ That incarnation body clearly belonged to Cleopatra, Egypt's ‘Last Pharaoh.’

[Who······ is Yoo Joonghyuk······?]

The next utterance of True Voice reverberated throughout the entire complex.

It was certainly an imposing display, but neither of us was intimidated. Cleopatra was only a Historical-grade constellation. Neither Yoo Joonghyuk nor I would cower before the mere aura of a Historical-grade constellation anymore.

“Yoo Joonghyuk. Can you win?”

With Story packs hanging all over my body, I could not handle her in my current condition. Yoo Joonghyuk shook his head.

“Not right now. It's almost that time.”

“You mean the penalty you mentioned? Disappearing for 10 minutes a day?”

Yoo Joonghyuk did not answer. Taking that as a yes, I turned to look at Cleopatra.

“Then what do we do about her······?”

“She won't be able to do anything.”

“Why?”

“Because the ‘Demon King Selection’ hasn't started yet.”

Naturally, the incarnation bodies of constellations who did not belong to this scenario were subject to severe probability restrictions. As long as the ‘Giant Story’ had not opened, they could not run amok as they pleased either.

But even so······.

“Hey, have you already forgotten what Asmodeus did to us?”

“Not everyone can act like Asmodeus.”

I knew that much.

In the Demon Realm, Demon Kings faced fewer probability restrictions than constellations. The problem was that those constellations had enough spare probability to overcome the restrictions.

“Cleopatra belongs to <Papyrus>, doesn't she? If she borrows her nebula's probability and wreaks havoc······.”

“Kim Dokja. You seem to have already forgotten what you did.”

“What?”

Before Yoo Joonghyuk could answer, Cleopatra's voice rang out through the air.

[The new ruler of this complex······ Tell him this. If he enters the Demon King Selection······ he will surely die.]

With those words, Cleopatra's incarnation body began to fade away.

Like an enormous sandcastle collapsing, the incarnation body crumbled into grains and returned to dust.

[Remember··· <Papyrus>··· never gives a second warning.]

But why was she leaving so meekly?

It was strange. After manifesting like that, these types usually considered massacring a few hundred incarnations no more than a little exercise after a meal.

Yoo Joonghyuk spoke as though he found me pathetic.

“Have you forgotten? They imposed [Fate] on you.”

“Ah.”

Come to think of it, that had happened.

Not just <Papyrus> but also <Vedas> and <Olympus> had poured enormous amounts of probability into declaring [Fate] in order to bring me over to their side.

So that was why Cleopatra had left without a fuss.

They were short on spare probability right now.

Yoo Joonghyuk spoke in his characteristically gloomy voice.

“That buys us time until the Demon King Selection.”

I nodded.

At least the constellations would not attack us right away.

I checked the message log.

[Preparations for the ‘Demon King Selection’ are underway.]

[Preparation time remaining: 28 days 17 hours 12 minutes]

If my prediction was correct, the ‘Demon King Selection’ would take up every scenario from number 21 through number 24. It was a Giant Story, so naturally it would eat up that many scenarios. Gauging the time we had left, I spoke.

“The two of us won't be enough.”

“I know.”

Once the Demon King Selection began, constellations would start appearing on the other side.

Even a Historical-grade constellation was far stronger than an ordinary incarnation once it reached the level of a constellation. Moreover, once the big names started appearing, Yoo Joonghyuk and I would have trouble facing them alone.

“Do you have anything in mind?”

Yoo Joonghyuk shook his head.

We could bring our companions over from Earth, but Lee Hyunsung and Jung Heewon were not yet strong enough to fight transcendents or constellations. They also needed time to grow stronger, alternating between personal scenarios and main scenarios. Only then could we properly deploy our forces in the later scenarios.

For now, we needed companions who could help us immediately.

“Haven't you gathered any companions here?”

“Ah, I have, but······.”

Come to think of it, where had Jang Hayoung gone?

I staggered as I looked around, my body aching.

“I actually asked someone to look for allies. It's about time there were some results······.”

“Get things ready. I'll be back shortly.”

Before I could ask where he was going, Yoo Joonghyuk vanished from sight.

●

To stretch my limbs and work out a plan, I roughly adjusted my bandages and left the treatment room.

Aileen had said I needed another 2 weeks of rest, but perhaps because the tension had eased, I did not feel all that bad.

[Your recovery ability is rising sharply due to the effect of the attribute ‘Lamarck’s Giraffe.’]

······Ah, it was the attribute's effect.

As I stepped outside with a casual stretch, a horrified Aileen rushed over.

I beat her to it before she could speak.

“I'm fine, so don't worry. Anyway, Aileen, could you fix this for me?”

Taking the Uriel doll from me, Aileen tilted her head.

“······What is this?”

“A constellation's symbolic body.”

Upon hearing that, Aileen committed the sacrilegious mistake of immediately dropping the doll.

Hurriedly picking it back up, Aileen looked at me and asked.

“······I won't receive divine punishment for dropping it, will I?”

“She's a kind constellation, so don't worry. Make sure the repairs hold.”

A kind constellation. It was a rather strange thing to say, but this was Uriel, after all, so the description probably wasn't so strange.

I said I would go for a short walk, then stepped out onto the streets of the industrial complex.

In the faint sunlight, the streets of the complex now had a distinctly different atmosphere.

A few people who recognized me gave slight nods as they passed.

Their faces held a vitality I had not seen before.

Perhaps these were the faces of people who had decided to live.

“Hey, Yoo Joonghyuk! You're awake?”

When I turned, the very person I had been looking for was running toward me.

With a running start, Jang Hayoung leaped up, clung to my neck, and put me in a clumsy headlock.

Struggling to pry Jang Hayoung off, I spoke.

“My name isn't Yoo Joonghyuk.”

“Ah, finally ready to reveal your real name?”

“······You knew?”

“Well, I figured I wasn't the only one using an alias.”

I looked at Jang Hayoung for a moment, then spoke in a meaningful tone.

“My name is Kim Dokja.”

I had tried to make it sound cool in my own way, but Jang Hayoung looked thoroughly unimpressed.

“What a weird name. I feel like I've heard it somewhere······.”

“······Never mind. What have you been doing all this time?”

“Ah, I was chatting for a while, then came out because there was a tip about this area.”

“A tip?”

“You've been lying in bed, so you wouldn't know, huh? A few interesting things have happened in the [Industrial Complex].”

Jang Hayoung told me what had happened over the past week. Of course, the most interesting part concerned Yoo Joonghyuk.

“He refused ‘ruling authority’?”

“Right. He said he'd inherit the title of duke, but wouldn't govern this place. That's why everyone's in an uproar.”

I could understand what was happening.

Yoo Joonghyuk was probably putting his motto, ‘Dominate, but do not reign,’ into practice. That was likely why he'd said such a thing. The idea was good. The situation was bad.

“The complex must be in chaos. Making a declaration like that before things are even settled will cause problems with public order.”

“Yeah, that's why the citizens are really worked up right now.”

A powerful dictator could control people's desires through his mere existence. But now that such a dictator had relinquished actual power, all the citizens' pent-up desires would begin to erupt at once.

「“Do you think the darkness of the industrial complex will disappear just because I die?”」

That was a line Duke Syswitz had spoken in ‘Ways of Survival.’

It struck me anew that he had been right.

Changing the ruler would not suddenly transform the entire [Industrial Complex]

Instead, with the tyrannical dictator gone, the desires people had concealed would reveal themselves even more starkly.

“Hey, hand over that fragment!”

“N-no. I picked it up.”

At the voices that rang out as though on cue, Jang Hayoung and I turned at the same time. Inside an alley, a group of men were beating an incarnation. The situation seemed obvious. They were surely fighting over a Story fragment from the [Factory].

Just as I was about to move, Jang Hayoung unexpectedly stopped me.

“Hold on. Wait a second.”

“······What?”

“I told you. There was a ‘tip.’”

“What tip?”

“The ‘Punisher’ is going to show up here.”

“The Punisher?”

I had never heard of anyone like that.

There was no such position in ‘Ways of Survival,’ nor in the ‘Revolutionary Scenario.’

Perhaps noticing my puzzlement, Jang Hayoung added.

“It's a nickname the citizens came up with. Someone who suddenly started appearing a few days ago, keeping the peace. An absolutely stunning······.”

At that moment, a man's shout came from inside the alley.

“Kill him and take it!”

The men drew their weapons, apparently preparing to turn the beating into something more serious.

It would be faster for me to act than to wait for some Punisher or whatever. Just as I reached for the sword at my waist, a slender shadow appeared in the alley.

“Stop.”

A woman wrapped in a black cape stood atop the wall.

The cape made it impossible to see exactly what weapons she carried, but her face was perfectly clear. A face that seemed to belong to a higher-resolution image than everyone else's. Watching her waist-length hair ripple in the wind, I slowly coaxed my thoughts through my overwhelming shock.

······Had there been someone like her in ‘Ways of Survival’?

Suddenly, it felt as though every word of praise I knew had lost its meaning.

Deep, delicate eyes beneath neat, ink-black brows.

Every standard by which the world judged beauty was collapsing at once.

A face that even the constellations' modifiers seemed unable to describe.

And so, infuriatingly, there was only one way to describe that face.

「Hers was undoubtedly a beauty that could put Yoo Joonghyuk to shame—by about three slaps' worth.」

Even ‘Ways of Survival’ had never used such an expression.

Even Jang Hayoung, whose looks ranked among the best in ‘Ways of Survival,’ was only ‘two slaps' worth’ better-looking than Yoo Joonghyuk. As I stood frozen in shock, the very person whose beauty outshone Yoo Joonghyuk by two slaps' worth whispered quietly.

“She's here. That's the Punisher.”

The men, who had also been overwhelmed by the woman's beauty, were belatedly coming to their senses. Judging by their leering mouths, what they were going to say seemed obvious. But before their mouths could open, something moved.

Thud, thud.

And something fell.

The men screamed a little later.

“A-aaargh!”

A man whose arm had been severed let out horrific screams. Then the others realized what had happened, hastily put away their weapons, and began to flee. They had recognized an enemy they could not fight.

Even the man she had saved ran out of the alley in terror. In an instant, only the woman and the men's severed arms remained.

Watching the woman quietly sheathe her sword, Jang Hayoung exclaimed in admiration.

“See? Isn't she freaking amazing? You told me to look for people who could help. I tried to talk to her yesterday, too, but she disappeared right away―”

Brutal in its execution, yet swordsmanship that still adhered to the prescribed path (定道).

What astonished me was the speed of that swordsmanship.

I murmured without realizing it.

“That isn't incarnation-level swordsmanship.”

“What?”

Jang Hayoung might not have noticed, but I had seen it clearly.

At this point, only transcendents could draw a sword that fast.

My heart pounded.

I did not know who this woman was, but if we could make her our companion now, she would undoubtedly be a tremendous asset in the ‘Demon King Selection.’

As the woman in the black cape began to turn away, I ran into the alley without hesitation.

“Hey!”

I planned to talk to her to buy time while using [Omniscient Reader's Viewpoint] to inspect her information. Whoever she was, if I could see her Attributes Window, persuading her would be easier.

And if I was lucky―

“Ghk······.”

But before I could approach her and use the skill, I had to stop in my tracks. The woman's blazing eyes were glaring at me. I trembled at the terrifying amount of emotion that reached me in that instant.

Immense resentment and anger directed at me.

It had been so long since I had experienced a torrent of emotion like that, I was momentarily stunned.

······What was with this woman?

Did she know me?

······More importantly, why did she hate me this much?

Barely pushing against the surging waves of resentment and anger, I shouted at the Punisher as she turned away.

“Hold on! Wait!”

But then the constellations' messages flooded into my head.

[The constellation ‘Prisoner of the Golden Headband’ is appalled.]

[A very small number of constellations are anxious about your judgment.]

[The constellation ‘Prisoner of the Golden Headband’ is having a violent allergic reaction to your perceptiveness.]

Huh? What?

What was this all of a sudden······?

[The constellation ‘Demon-like Judge of Fire’ has entered the channel.]

······Ah, Uriel!

[The constellation ‘Demon-like Judge of Fire’ is appalled!]

[The constellation ‘Demon-like Judge of Fire’ is appalled!]

[The constellation ‘Demon-like Judge of Fire’ is appalled!]

A whole week had already passed since the incident with Asmodeus, so it was not strange for Uriel to enter the channel again. The problem was the constellations' messages that followed.

[The constellation ‘Demon-like Judge of Fire’ asks how on earth this happened.]

[The constellation ‘Prisoner of the Golden Headband’ says he doesn't really know either.]

[A constellation who enjoys sex changes snickers.]

[The constellation ‘Demon-like Judge of Fire’ points an accusing finger at the nebula ‘Asgard.’]

The sudden flood of messages from the constellations left me unable to think straight.

What on earth was going on?

Why point a finger······?

While I was bewildered by the constellations' messages, the Punisher quickly vanished from the alley.

“Hey, I said wait!”

What a shame. It had been a chance to gain a good companion.

Jang Hayoung, who had caught up belatedly, chimed in.

“Well? Isn't she incredibly pretty?”

“When did she start appearing?”

“Three or four days ago. She's not just beautiful, she's amazingly skilled, too, so word spread in no time. And she comes and goes like a ghost.”

“Will she come tomorrow, too?”

I had not identified the style of her swordsmanship, but a sword draw like that would certainly be a great help in the ‘Demon King Selection.’

Still, where had someone like her come from? She definitely hadn't been in the original ‘Ways of Survival’······.

“She's come every day, so she'll probably come tomorrow, too. Anyway, looks like you've fallen hard, huh?”

“It's not like that.”

“I'm kidding, kidding. I know. You don't like women.”

“······Who said that?”

Where had another ridiculous rumor like that come from······?

[The constellation ‘Demon-like Judge of Fire’ looks at you.]

······I think I know where that ridiculous rumor came from.

“It's been a while, Uriel.”

●

[The constellation ‘Demon-like Judge of Fire’ gives an ‘ahem’ and sticks her nose in the air.]

Listening to Uriel's intermittent indirect messages, I headed toward the treatment room with Jang Hayoung.

[The constellation ‘Demon-like Judge of Fire’ praises her own achievements.]

Most of what I heard was an account of Uriel's reckless adventures after persuading Yoo Joonghyuk to visit the Demon Realm with her.

So it really had been Uriel who persuaded Yoo Joonghyuk to save me.

I had thought as much.

There was no way that bastard would have come here of his own accord to save me.

“Your symbolic body is being repaired. Once it's done, you'll be able to manifest through it again.”

[The constellation ‘Demon-like Judge of Fire’ is moved to tears.]

“But what personal scenario did you give Yoo Joonghyuk? It must be dangerous for an archangel to issue a personal scenario in the Demon Realm so carelessly.”

In fact, it was dangerous for a high-ranking constellation of Uriel's caliber to come to the Demon Realm.

The nebula <Eden> and the Demon Realm of the 72 Demon Kings were in a state of truce.

That was probably part of the reason Uriel had manifested through a shabby symbolic body instead of a proper incarnation body. If not for those circumstances, Uriel would probably never have been so helpless against Asmodeus in the first place.

[The constellation ‘Demon-like Judge of Fire’ looks dejected.]

[The constellation ‘Demon-like Judge of Fire’ says that none of that matters anymore anyway.]

Come to think of it, when the link between Yoo Joonghyuk and Uriel broke, Uriel's personal scenario would have been forcibly erased.

Yoo Joonghyuk had also said he had received another personal scenario.

That was when Jang Hayoung, who had been quietly listening to my conversation with Uriel, interrupted.

“But how are you so close to the constellations?”

“I'm a constellation, too.”

“······What? You're joking, right?”

“Didn't I tell you?”

Jang Hayoung spoke with a somewhat conflicted expression.

“A constellation······ You mean one of those things in the sky, right? Like that mummy that showed up this morning.”

“Usually, yes.”
